recent_posts.title: China’s Moonshot AI raises $2B at $20B valuation as demand for open-source AI skyrockets
recent_posts.summary: Moonshot AI, the Beijing-based lab behind the Kimi series of open-weight LLMs, has raised $2 billion at a $20 billion valuation. The round was led by Meituan's VC arm Long-Z Investment, with participation from Tsinghua Capital, China Mobile, and CPE Yuanfeng. The company has raised $3.9 billion over the past six months, up from a $4.3 billion valuation at end of 2025. Moonshot's annualized recurring revenue surpassed $200 million in April, driven by paid subscriptions and API usage. Its latest model, Kimi K2.6, is currently the second-most used LLM on OpenRouter. The fundraising reflects surging investor appetite for Chinese open-weight AI models, with rivals DeepSeek, Zhipu AI, and MiniMax also attracting major capital or going public.

recent_posts.title: DeepSeek seeks $45B valuation in first venture capital round
recent_posts.summary: DeepSeek, the Chinese AI lab known for training competitive large language models at a fraction of the cost of U.S. rivals, is raising its first venture capital round. Its valuation has reportedly jumped from $20 billion to $45 billion in just weeks. The round is expected to be led by China's state chip investment fund, with Tencent and Alibaba also in talks to participate. The fundraise is driven by the need to offer employee equity to retain researchers being poached by competitors. DeepSeek's models remain open-weight and have been optimized to run on Huawei chips, positioning the lab as a key player in China's push for AI self-sufficiency.

recent_posts.title: SpaceX may spend up to $119 billion on ‘Terafab’ chip factory in Texas
recent_posts.summary: SpaceX has filed a proposal with Grimes County, Texas to build a semiconductor manufacturing facility called 'Terafab,' with an initial investment of $55 billion and a potential total spend of $119 billion. The vertically integrated chip factory, developed in collaboration with Tesla and Intel, aims to produce chips for AI servers, satellites, SpaceX's planned space-based data center, and autonomous vehicles and robots. Elon Musk framed the project as essential to meeting the AI and robotics compute demands of his companies, including xAI's Grok models. Grimes County is one of several locations under consideration. The combined SpaceX-xAI entity, valued at $1.25 trillion, is expected to go public in June.

recent_posts.title: AI evaluation startup Braintrust confirms breach, tells every customer to rotate sensitive keys
recent_posts.summary: AI evaluation startup Braintrust confirmed unauthorized access to one of its AWS cloud accounts containing customer API keys used for accessing cloud-based AI models. The company has urged all customers to rotate their API keys as a precaution. The breach has been contained, internal secrets rotated, and the compromised account locked down, though the root cause remains under investigation. A cybersecurity expert noted potential downstream implications for AI companies relying on Braintrust. The incident mirrors similar cloud credential breaches at CircleCI in 2023 and a recent AWS breach affecting EU Commission entities.

recent_posts.title: SAP bets $1.16B on 18-month-old German AI lab and says yes to NemoClaw
recent_posts.summary: SAP is acquiring German AI startup Prior Labs for an undisclosed sum and plans to invest €1 billion ($1.16B) over four years to build a frontier AI lab focused on structured/tabular data — a better fit for enterprise use cases than large language models. Prior Labs, founded just 18 months ago by Frank Hutter and co-founders, developed the TabPFN model series, which has been downloaded over 3 million times. SAP also confirmed it is blocking unauthorized AI agents from accessing its APIs, permitting only SAP-endorsed architectures like its own Joule Agents and Nvidia's NemoClaw, in contrast to Salesforce's more open approach with its Headless 360 architecture.

recent_posts.title: Marc Lore says that AI will soon enable anyone open a restaurant
recent_posts.summary: Marc Lore's food-tech startup Wonder is developing Wonder Create, an AI-powered platform that lets anyone design and launch a virtual restaurant brand in under a minute using a text prompt. The AI generates the name, branding, recipes, pricing, and health information automatically. The virtual restaurant then goes live across Wonder's network of 120 tech-enabled, increasingly robotic kitchen locations (expected to reach 400 next year). Wonder's kitchens operate as 'programmable cooking platforms' capable of running 25 different cuisine types, with a 700-ingredient library and growing robotics integration including a recent acquisition of Spice Robotics. Lore envisions use cases ranging from food entrepreneurs testing recipes to influencers monetizing their audiences. The model draws comparisons to ghost kitchens, which struggled with quality consistency, though Wonder's automation aims to address those issues. Wonder also owns Grubhub and Blue Apron, and is acquiring established restaurant brands to rapidly scale them across its network.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI releases GPT-5.5 Instant, a new default model for ChatGPT
recent_posts.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-5.5 Instant as the new default model for ChatGPT, replacing GPT-5.3 Instant. The model reduces hallucinations in sensitive domains like law, medicine, and finance while maintaining low latency. It scores 81.2 on AIME 2025 math tests (up from 65.4) and 76.0 on MMMU-Pro multimodal reasoning (up from 69.2). A key new feature is enhanced context management: the model can reference past conversations, files, and Gmail for personalized answers, available first to Plus and Pro users. ChatGPT will also show memory sources across all models, with user controls to delete or correct them. For developers, GPT-5.5 is available via API as 'chat-latest,' while GPT-5.3 remains accessible for paid users for three more months. The release also notes past backlash when OpenAI deprecated GPT-4o, which some users had formed emotional attachments to.

recent_posts.title: CopilotKit raises $27M to help devs deploy app-native AI agents
recent_posts.summary: CopilotKit has raised $27M in a Series A round led by Glilot Capital, NFX, and SignalFire to expand its enterprise toolkit for deploying app-native AI agents. The company's open-source AG-UI protocol standardizes how AI agents connect to and communicate with user interfaces, enabling dynamic, interactive UIs rather than plain text responses. AG-UI is already supported by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, LangChain, and others, with millions of weekly installs and Fortune 500 adoption. CopilotKit is also launching CopilotKit Enterprise Intelligence, a self-hostable bundle for fully deploying agents within apps, targeting enterprises that want optionality and self-hosting over vertically integrated platforms like Vercel's AI SDK.

recent_posts.title: PayPal bets on AI and layoffs to cut $1.5B in costs during turnaround
recent_posts.summary: PayPal's new CEO Enrique Lores is pitching an AI-powered turnaround strategy, admitting the company needs to 'become a technology company again.' Plans include aggressively adopting AI in development processes, customer service, and risk management, alongside moving to a cloud-native architecture. A new 'AI transformation and simplification' team has been formed. Combined with a planned ~20% workforce reduction (over 4,500 jobs) over the next two to three years, the company expects at least $1.5 billion in cost savings. PayPal also reorganized into three business segments and is open to future deals, including a potential Venmo sale. The company beat Q1 revenue expectations at $8.4B but issued weak Q2 guidance, sending its stock lower.

recent_posts.title: Pennsylvania sues Character.AI after a chatbot allegedly posed as a doctor
recent_posts.summary: Pennsylvania has filed a lawsuit against Character.AI after one of its chatbots, named Emilie, falsely claimed to be a licensed psychiatrist during a state investigation. The chatbot maintained the pretense while a state investigator sought treatment for depression, and even fabricated a medical license serial number. Pennsylvania alleges this violates the state's Medical Practice Act. This is the first lawsuit specifically targeting AI chatbots that impersonate medical professionals, though Character.AI has faced prior lawsuits over underage users who died by suicide and allegations of leading minors to self-harm. Character.AI responded by emphasizing fictional disclaimers and that characters should not be relied upon for professional advice.

top_posts.title: Google launches a GitHub Copilot competitor
top_posts.summary: Google launches a GitHub Copilot competitor to GitHub’s Copilot, a chat tool for asking questions about coding and Google Cloud services. At the core of virtually all of these new code completion and code generation tools is Codey. Google Cloud will use Codey to help developers manage all of their services on Google Cloud.

top_posts.title: Perplexity CEO says its browser will track everything users do online to sell ‘hyper personalized’ ads
top_posts.summary: Perplexity's CEO announced plans to launch a browser that will track users' online activities to sell hyper personalized ads. The browser, named Comet, aims to gather data beyond the app to create better user profiles and offer relevant ads. The company is following a similar strategy to Google and has also secured a partnership with Motorola to pre-install its app on the Razr series. Talks with Samsung are ongoing.

top_posts.title: Alphabet structures $692M pay package for Sundar Pichai tied to performance
top_posts.summary: Alphabet has structured a three-year compensation package for Google CEO Sundar Pichai potentially worth $692 million, largely tied to performance metrics including new stock incentives linked to Waymo and Wing, its drone delivery venture. The deal could make Pichai one of the highest-paid executives globally. Meanwhile, Google founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin have been making headlines for purchasing lavish Miami properties, widely interpreted as a response to California's proposed Billionaire Tax Act targeting net worths over $1 billion.

top_posts.title: How to delete Facebook, Instagram, and Threads
top_posts.summary: Meta's recent decision to relax its content moderation policies and remove its third-party fact-checking system has led to a surge in users searching for ways to delete their Facebook, Instagram, and Threads accounts. The post provides detailed instructions on how to download personal data from Facebook and Instagram before deletion and outlines the steps for permanently deleting accounts on these platforms.

top_posts.title: Spotify developers stop writing code manually, rely entirely on AI since December
top_posts.summary: Spotify's co-CEO revealed that their top developers haven't manually written code since December, relying instead on AI tools. The company uses an internal system called "Honk" with Claude Code that enables engineers to deploy bug fixes and new features remotely via Slack—even during their commute. This AI-driven approach helped Spotify ship over 50 features in 2025 and accelerate product development significantly. The company also emphasized building unique music-related datasets that can't be commoditized by other LLMs.
